questions.text:
Consider the sequential circuit shown in the figure, where both flip-flops used are positive edge-triggered D flip-flops.

The number of states in the state transition diagram of this circuit that have a transition back to the same state on some value of "in" is _____.
questions.solution:
The two D flip-flops form a shift register: next state ([latex]Q_1,Q_2[/latex]) = (in, [latex]Q_1[/latex]). A state goes back to itself only if in = [latex]Q_1[/latex] = [latex]Q_2[/latex]: state 00 (with in = 0) and state 11 (with in = 1).

Answer: 2

questions.text: A 32-bit wide main memory unit with a capacity of 1 GB is built using 256M x 4-bit DRAM chips. The number of rows of memory cells in the DRAM chip is [latex]2^{14}[/latex]. The time taken to perform one refresh operation is 50 nanoseconds. The refresh period is 2 milliseconds. The percentage (rounded to the closest integer) of the time available for performing the memory read/write operations in the main memory unit is __________.
questions.solution:
Each 256M [latex]\times[/latex] 4 chip refreshes its [latex]2^{14}[/latex] rows one at a time: [latex]2^{14}\times50[/latex] ns = 819.2 [latex]\mu[/latex]s in every 2 ms (all chips refresh in parallel).

Refresh takes 0.8192 / 2 = 40.96% of the time, leaving about 59% for reads and writes.

Answer: 59

questions.text: Consider a system with 3 processes that share 4 instances of the same resource type. Each process can request a maximum of K instances. Resource instances can be requested and released only one at a time. The largest value of K that will always avoid deadlock is ____.
questions.solution:
Deadlock is impossible if, even when every process holds K [latex]-[/latex] 1 instances, one instance is still free: [latex]3(K-1)+1\le4\Rightarrow K\le2[/latex].

With K = 3, two processes could hold 2 each and wait forever.

Answer: 2

questions.text: Consider a long-lived TCP session with an end-to-end bandwidth of 1 Gbps (= [latex]10^{9} [/latex] bits-per-second). The session starts with a sequence number of 1234. The minimum time (in seconds, rounded to the closest integer) before this sequence number can be used again is _______.
questions.solution:
TCP numbers bytes with 32-bit sequence numbers, so they wrap after [latex]2^{32}[/latex] bytes.
Time = [latex]\frac{2^{32}\times8}{10^9}\approx34.36[/latex] s [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 34 s.

Answer: 34
